PEP screening shall use credible commercial databases and risk-based enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons, irrespective of nationality.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies House e-Registry (Gibraltar Financial Services Commission integrated company registry portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin alphabet, are generally submitted in English, and may include Romanized transliteration if sourced from non-Latin script. The name must be distinct from existing Gibraltar companies, must not be misleading, and must comply with Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 Section 28 on prohibited names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may submit a written appeal to the Registrar of Companies within 14 calendar days, setting out grounds for reconsideration. The appeal may be supported by legal submissions proving non-confliction and non-misleading nature. If rejected at administrative appeal, the applicant may apply to the Gibraltar Supreme Court for judicial review within 28 days, or re-file a fresh name reservation request using a modified name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office in Gibraltar is mandatory; a pure virtual office is not permitted as the registered office. However, the registered agent's address in Gibraltar can be used for statutory registered office purposes, provided day-to-day management and commercial substance may be elsewhere. For a low-risk distribution entity with no physical premises in Gibraltar, remote management is acceptable subject to substance reporting, but the registered office must remain a physical address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% quantified risk of unannounced on-site inspection for a low-risk, non-regulated distribution company; likelihood increases if the registered agent is under regulatory review or if inconsistencies arise in UBO filings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (Cap. 213), Sections 5–21 (incorporation, memorandum and articles, registration), Section 8 (name restrictions), and Sections 19–20 (certificate of incorporation); Income Tax Act 2010, Sections 8 and 40B (non-resident tax-exempt status for exempted companies) as domesticated for the Cayman-style Exempted Company template under Gibraltar law
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Gibraltar Companies House, Registry of Companies, Ministry of Commerce (H.M. Government of Gibraltar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Form CO1) together with executed Memorandum and Articles of Association and declaration of compliance, filed with the Registrar of Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account requirement. The company may be incorporated with a single ordinary share of USD 1.00 at par, fully subscribed and credited as paid. Share capital may be denominated in USD or any freely convertible currency. Tax-exempt non-resident status requires a statutory declaration that control and management of the company are exercised outside Gibraltar and that no trading activity is carried on within Gibraltar.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscription of one ordinary share of USD 1.00 at par by the founding subscriber be and is hereby ratified and recorded in the Register of Members; RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby established at the premises of the licensed corporate services provider in Gibraltar, which is appointed as Registered Office Provider; RESOLVED that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as first Director and [Name] as Company Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting; RESOLVED that the Directors be and are hereby authorised to open bank and payment accounts, execute organic matcha procurement and distribution agreements, and make all ancillary filings under the Companies Act 2014 and applicable trade regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Clearance and Legal Structure Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House, Registry of Companies (online name search portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search and reservation application through the Gibraltar Companies House online portal for the proposed entity name. Verify that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, does not contain prohibited words, and is acceptable under the Companies Act name restrictions. Confirm that the name reflects the exempted-company nature and matches the composite jurisdictional key (GB/GI/KY). Upon approval, obtain a name reservation certificate valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (1 primary and 2 alternatives)
Applicant shareholder or subscriber passport copy
Letter of intent confirming Gibraltar exempted company form
Draft memorandum of association
Licensed registered agent acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as undesirable or too similar, file a revised name submission within 5 working days; alternatively, request an internal reconsideration from the Registrar under Section 8(2) of the Companies Act 2014, with supporting evidence of distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing with Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House, Registry of Companies (submission desk / e-portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute and file the Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form CO1 (Application for Registration) and the statutory declaration of compliance. Pay the official state filing fee of USD 250 (or GIP equivalent). Ensure the registered office address is stated as the licensed corporate services provider's premises and first director/secretary consents are attached. The Registrar will review the application, after which the Certificate of Incorporation is issued.
required_dossiers: Form CO1 — Application for Registration of a Company
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Form CO2 — Consent of Director and Company Secretary
Statutory declaration of compliance under the Companies Act 2014
Registered office consent letter
Receipt of state filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or rejection notice, cure the stated deficiency within 21 days by re-filing the corrected Form CO1 or amended Memorandum and Articles. A rectification re-submission is expedited within 3 working days upon payment of a 10% re-filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Tax-Exempt (Non-Resident) Election
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House and the Gibraltar Commissioner of Income Tax (via licensed corporate services provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, file the election and statutory declaration for non-resident tax-exempt status under the Income Tax Act 2010. This includes evidence that central management and control, board meetings, and executive decision-making will occur outside Gibraltar. Submit the board resolution adopting the exempt status and maintain a minute of non-residence declaration in the statutory books. Obtain the Certificate of Tax-Exempt Status issued by the Commissioner of Income Tax.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (registry-issued)
Statutory declaration of non-residence in Gibraltar
Written election for tax-exempt status under Section 40B Income Tax Act 2010
First board resolution approving the exempt status election
CSP confirmation of external management and control
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commissioner of Income Tax questions the exempt status, file supplementary evidence of offshore management and control within 30 days; request an appeal or written opinion from the Income Tax Tribunal if the determination is adverse, with the company continuing to be treated as exempt pending resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Adoption, Statutory Registers, and Beneficial Ownership Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House (Registrar of Beneficial Ownership) and licensed corporate services provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the registered office at the licensed corporate services provider's Gibraltar address. Prepare and maintain the statutory registers (members, directors, secretary, charges). File the beneficial ownership return with the Gibraltar Registrar of Beneficial Ownership (GRBOR) within the statutory deadline, identifying the ultimate beneficial owner. Complete AML/KYC due diligence with the corporate services provider and record the Certificate of Incumbency for the exempted company.
required_dossiers: Registered office consent letter and service agreement
First board minutes adopting registered office and statutory registers
Beneficial ownership register return (GRBOR filing form)
AML/KYC pack: passport, proof of address, source of funds for UBO
Certificate of Incumbency request form
Director and secretary consents and identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the GRBOR filing is queried or flagged, correct the beneficial ownership data within 14 days by filing an amended return; failure to remedy attracts a daily penalty of GIP 100. For any corporate register defect, apply for a rectification order from the Registrar under the Companies Act 2014.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Government Department for Enterprise and Trade; local advisory oversight by the Gibraltar Trading Standards Division (no industry-specific licence applicable to pure wholesale matcha distribution)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific operating licence required for ISIC 4631 cross-border procurement and wholesale distribution of organic matcha powder. Optional Food Business Registration (FBR) under the Food Safety Act 2014 is advisable if the company maintains a local storage or fulfilment point in Gibraltar. No excise, manufacturing, or processing permit applies as the commercial model is limited to trading and distribution with no on-site conversion.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Gibraltar Department of Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change (DESCC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 3 (minor commercial activity without physical development). No full EIA or screening opinion required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations 2018 because the activity involves no construction, no land disturbance, and no industrial processing facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A for pure trading activities. If bonded or third-party warehousing is later established in Gibraltar, compliance with the Water Pollution Act 1995 is required for any point-source discharge, and waste handling must meet the EU-approved Gibraltar residual waste retention standards. All imported organic matcha packaging must be food-contact compliant under EC 1935/2004 and, where introduced to the Gibraltar market, recyclable or compostable per EN 13432.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance under the Fire Safety (Premises) Regulations 2019 and structural load integrity inspection per BS EN 15635 for any storage racking if a local fulfilment hub is operated; occupancy and workplace safety clearance from the Gibraltar Safety at Work Inspectorate under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2012 is required before personnel are present at any Gibraltar location. In the default no-premises model, only a registered office at the licensed CSP is maintained, with no physical clearance triggered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar - Department of Taxation (Commissioner of Income Tax), official tax portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation; customs and excise administration: HM Customs & Excise, Gibraltar. (UK VAT, administered by HM Revenue & Customs, does not extend to Gibraltar.)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Cayman Exempted Company is not registrable in Gibraltar for income tax unless it is managed and controlled (M&C) in Gibraltar or carries on activity through a Gibraltar permanent establishment (PE). If registration is triggered: (1) file Company Registration form IT-1 (non-Gibraltar company) with the Department of Taxation within 30 days of commencement; (2) attach the Cayman Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing, Memorandum and Articles, register of directors/members, UBO declaration, Gibraltar service address, and board resolutions adopting the tax classification; (3) obtain the Gibraltar TIN (company tax reference) from the Commissioner, which is issued within 5 business days of complete filing and is used for all corporate tax, CRS and FATCA reporting; no minimum capital is required; (4) if a branch is constituted, file form EBR-1 with the Gibraltar Companies Registry and obtain the branch number; (5) file annual returns (Form C) thereafter and update the ITD on PE activities. The Cayman-side tax registration requirement is limited to the 20-year Exempted Company tax-exemption certificate under Cayman law; no Cayman income-tax TIN is issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Gibraltar. The relevant statutory elections are: (i) Qualifying Company (QC) election under the Qualifying (Companies and Individuals) Rules 2011 - 2% tax rate on qualifying offshore profits, subject to economic substance, 80% non-domestic income cap and a minimum annual tax of £1,000; (ii) branch separate-entity election under the Income Tax Act 2010 s.19(8) for loss-relief and treaty allocation; (iii) group relief election under the Income Tax (Group Relief) Rules for 75%+ groups; (iv) UK anti-hybrid classification statements under TIOPA 2010 Part 6A where inconsistent opacity/transparency between UK and Gibraltar/Cayman treatment exists; and (v) non-resident 'no PE' declaration for the avoidance of doubt. The pre-2011 Gibraltar 'tax-exempt company' route is closed; the Cayman entity's exemption derives solely from its Cayman tax-exempt status and absence of Gibraltar-residing management and control.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (monetary authority for sterling) jointly with the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) (banking licensing, prudential and AML/CFT supervision of Gibraltar banks); the Government of Gibraltar issues Gibraltar pound (GIP) banknotes pegged at par to GBP. For the Cayman Islands exempted company, the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (CIMA) has regulatory oversight of the corporate services provider and AML regime, but holds no exchange control function.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full capital and current account convertibility. The UK and Gibraltar have maintained complete freedom of exchange controls since 1979. The Gibraltar pound is convertible at par with sterling; no licensing, exchange approval, or repatriation permit is required for profit remittance, dividend distribution, loan repayments, or capital outflows from either jurisdiction. For the Cayman exempted company, the Cayman Islands impose no exchange controls and no withholding taxes on dividends, interest, or royalty flows. Practical hurdles are limited to documentary compliance (beneficial ownership attestations, board resolutions, tax residency statements, FATCA/CRS registration) and bank KYC rather than statutory approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or repatriation requirement exists in the UK, Gibraltar, or the Cayman Islands. Export proceeds from organic matcha powder sales are freely retainable in any convertible currency (USD, EUR, JPY, GBP, or offshore CNH). There is no mandatory conversion ratio, no mandated holding period, and no statutory deadline for converting or remitting export receipts. Treasury policy may nonetheless elect to draw down FX forward lines to hedge JPY/EUR exposures.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH, subject to conditionality. UK-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (e.g., Wise Platform and Revolut Business, regulated by the FCA under the Electronic Money Regulations 2011) will generally onboard a Cayman exempted company engaged in low-risk physical goods trade, provided the Cayman beneficial ownership register is current and UBEO documentation is complete. Legal constraints: EMIs are not deposit-taking banks, offer no FSCS-style deposit protection, and maintain client funds in safeguarded accounts; they cannot issue commercial letters of credit or provide credit/hedging lines. The EMI route is recommended as a tactical multi-currency operating rail (SWIFT TT and GBP Faster Payments) alongside a regulated Gibraltar bank account for settlement finality, escrow capacity, and documentary trade services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar-licensed banks generally require an in-person onboarding interview for offshore-incorporated clients; at least one director or the appointed authorised signatory must attend at the bank's Gibraltar branch. Banco de Sabadell and NatWest may accept a video KYC interview where the signatory is introduced by a regulated UK/Gibraltar professional (law firm or fiduciary) and all corporate documents are legalised/apostilled; a secondary face-to-face meeting with the ultimate beneficial owner may be required in cases of non-UK residency. Remote-only onboarding without an introducer is not a standard market practice for a Cayman exempted company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman exempted company exhibiting no demonstrable economic substance in either Cayman or Gibraltar
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cayman Economic Substance Notification and Register of Directors filed with CIMA; Certificate of Tax Exemption; Gibraltar substance roadmap (registered office, licensed local accountant, retained business records); ISIC 4631 wholesale distribution model documentation (procurement contracts, offtake agreements); group organisational chart showing commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity through bearer shares, nominee holdings, or incomplete UBEO records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cayman Islands Beneficial Ownership Register (BOR) extract; certificate of incumbency from the licensed registered agent; shareholder register and issued share ledger; UBEO passport and proof of residential address; tax identification numbers and CRS/FATCA self-certifications for all natural persons at 25% or greater.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdiction mismatch: Cayman-incorporated entity seeking to bank in Gibraltar for UK/EU trade flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed procurement and distribution contracts for culinary and ceremonial matcha powder; UK/EU logistics and warehousing appointments; target payment rails narrative (SWIFT TT and wire transfer); tax structuring opinion from admitted Gibraltar and Cayman counsel confirming no regulatory arbitrage beyond commercially justified interposition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and CFT exposure on East Asian supplier payment corridor (Japan and offshore CNY to China)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier due diligence files (certificate of incorporation, bank statement validation, beneficial ownership of supplier); organic certification records (JAS, EU Organic, USDA NOP where applicable); purchase orders, commercial invoices, packing lists and bills of lading; UN/EU/HMT sanctions screening reports; per-transaction value benchmarks consistent with wholesale matcha market data.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds ambiguity for initial capital injection from non-institutional shareholder accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of shareholder bank statements; executed share subscription agreement and board minutes authorising the capital contribution; completed source-of-wealth questionnaire; supporting tax returns or net-worth certificate; declaration confirming no crypto, gambling, or third-party funding source.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires (1) Cayman board resolution and share subscription agreement; (2) remittance via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own regulated bank account to the designated Gibraltar operational account, or to a licensed fiduciary escrow account where capital escrow staging is required; (3) full payment narrative identifying the exempted company's legal name, Cayman registered office, and reference 'Capital contribution – subscription for ordinary shares'; (4) when routed through a UK EMI, settlement via Faster Payments for GBP or SWIFT TT for USD/EUR/JPY with an identical purpose reference; (5) the receiving Gibraltar bank must obtain the share subscription agreement, source-of-funds evidence, and UBEO declaration before the funds are released for operational use; (6) all steps must satisfy the customer due diligence standards under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar) and applicable Payment Services Regulations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for organic matcha powder procurement are executed through: (a) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for standard open-account supplier payments in JPY, offshore CNY (CNH), USD, or EUR; (b) irrevocable documentary letters of credit under UCP600 (SWIFT MT700) for first-time or large-volume Japanese and Chinese supplier relationships; (c) UK Faster Payments or CHAPS for GBP payments to domestic logistics and quality-certification providers; (d) SEPA Instant for EUR disbursements to Gibraltar, EU, and EEA freight and warehousing counterparties; (e) every disbursement must be matched to a commercial invoice, purchase order, organic certificate, and transport document to satisfy AML transaction-purpose reviews.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla outright FX forwards (tenor up to 12 months; GBP/JPY, USD/JPY, EUR/JPY, GBP/EUR) matched to anticipated trade cash flows
FX swaps (spot-start/forward-maturity principal and interest swap) for rolling JPY and EUR procurement exposure without embedded leverage
Offshore Chinese renminbi (CNH) non-deliverable forwards (NDFs), cash-settled in USD, for mainland China organic matcha supplier settlements
Cross-currency swaps (GBP/EUR, USD/JPY) limited to hedge accounting alignment with underlying procurement and offtake contracts

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% (Gibraltar corporate income tax) / 0% (Cayman Islands, exempted company status)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Gibraltar: no capital gains tax; exemption for qualifying dividend income; 100% first-year capital allowances on plant and machinery; R&D additional deduction; group relief for Gibraltar-resident affiliates; 0% withholding tax on outbound payments. A Cayman Exempted Company that is managed and controlled in Gibraltar is taxed on worldwide income at 12.5%; if it instead maintains management and control in the Cayman Islands and has no Gibraltar PE, effective rate is 0% but dual economic substance exposure arises. Trading losses are recognised against future profits of the same trade (statutory review window of 5 years), subject to the 70% annual offset cap applicable to carried-forward losses.
